143	def weighted_roc_auc(y_true, y_prob):
144	    """Weighted one-vs-rest ROC AUC that also copes with two class problems."""
145	    y_prob = np.asarray(y_prob)
146	    if y_prob.ndim == 1:
147	        return roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob, average="weighted")
148	    if y_prob.shape[1] == 1:
149	        return roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob[:, 0], average="weighted")
150	    if y_prob.shape[1] == 2 and len(np.unique(np.asarray(y_true))) <= 2:
151	        return roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob[:, 1], average="weighted")
152	    return roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob, multi_class="ovr", average="weighted")

157	    available = (estimator if estimator is not None else AdaBoostClassifier()).get_params()

164	            remapped[base_name + '__' + key.split('__', 1)[1]] = value

    dims = [i for i in range(1, n_features + 1)]
    seeds = [random_seed + i for i in range(5)]

    errors = defaultdict(dict)
    for dim, seed in product(dims, seeds):

def init_analysis(X, y, n_clusters, filename):
    # Number of run (with randomly generated dataset) for each strategy so as
    # to be able to compute an estimate of the standard deviation
    n_runs = 5

    # k-means models can do several random inits so as to be able to trade
    # CPU time for convergence robustness
    n_init_range = np.array([1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 50, 75, 100])

    # Part 1: Quantitative evaluation of various init methods

    plt.figure()
    plots = []
    legends = []

    cases = [
        (KMeans, 'k-means++', {}),
        (KMeans, 'random', {}),
        (MiniBatchKMeans, 'k-means++', {'max_no_improvement': 3}),
        (MiniBatchKMeans, 'random', {'max_no_improvement': 3, 'init_size': 500}),
    ]

    for factory, init, params in cases:
        print("Evaluation of %s with %s init" % (factory.__name__, init))
        inertia = np.empty((len(n_init_range), n_runs))

def bench_EM(estimator, labels, name, data, sample_size, n_clusters, random_state, filename, verbose=False):
    t0 = time()
    estimator.fit(data)
    fit_time = time() - t0

    preds = estimator.predict(data)

    homo = metrics.homogeneity_score(labels, preds)
    comp = metrics.completeness_score(labels, preds)
    v_meas = metrics.v_measure_score(labels, preds)
    ari = metrics.adjusted_rand_score(labels, preds)
    ami = metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score(labels, preds)
    fks = metrics.fowlkes_mallows_score(labels, preds)
    silo = metrics.silhouette_score(data, preds, metric='euclidean', sample_size=sample_size,
                                    random_state=random_state)
    dbs = metrics.davies_bouldin_score(data, preds)
    chs = metrics.calinski_harabasz_score(data, preds)
    aics = estimator.aic(data)  # Akaike information criterion for the current model on the input X. Lower is better
    bics = estimator.bic(data)  # Bayesian information criterion for the current model on the input X. Lower is Better
    scor = estimator.score(data)
    if verbose:
        print('%-9s\t%d\t%.2fs\t%.2f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%i\t%i\t%i\t%.3f'
              % (name, n_clusters, fit_time, homo, comp, v_meas, ari, ami, fks, silo, dbs, chs, aics, bics, scor)
              )
    return fit_time, homo, comp, v_meas, ari, ami, fks, silo, dbs, chs, aics, bics, scor

import os

import numpy as np

import util
import clustering
from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture

X, y = util.data_load_no_split('Mobile_Prices.csv', 'price_range', scalar=1)
print('full data', X.shape, type(X).__name__, 'classes', sorted(np.unique(y)))

Xs = X.iloc[:300].reset_index(drop=True)
ys = y.iloc[:300].reset_index(drop=True)
print('sub data', Xs.shape)

# ---- bench_k_means parity
km = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=1)
out = clustering.bench_k_means(km, labels=ys, name='k-means++', data=Xs, sample_size=400,
                               n_clusters=4, random_state=1, filename='Mobile_Prices', verbose=True)
print('kmeans tuple len', len(out))
print('all finite', all(np.isfinite(v) for v in out))
print('values', [round(float(v), 6) for v in out])

ref = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=1).fit(Xs)
p = ref.predict(Xs)
expected = (metrics.homogeneity_score(ys, p),
            metrics.completeness_score(ys, p),
            metrics.v_measure_score(ys, p),
            metrics.adjusted_rand_score(ys, p),
            metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score(ys, p),
            metrics.fowlkes_mallows_score(ys, p),
            metrics.silhouette_score(Xs, p, metric='euclidean', sample_size=400, random_state=1),
            metrics.davies_bouldin_score(Xs, p),
            metrics.calinski_harabasz_score(Xs, p),

    print('   %-5s %.10f %.10f %s' % (nm, a, b, abs(a - b) < 1e-12))

# ---- bench_EM parity
gm = GaussianMixture(n_components=4, covariance_type='tied', n_init=1, random_state=1)
out2 = clustering.bench_EM(gm, labels=ys, name='tied', data=Xs, sample_size=400,
                           n_clusters=4, random_state=1, filename='Mobile_Prices', verbose=True)
print('EM tuple len', len(out2))
print('all finite', all(np.isfinite(v) for v in out2))

ref2 = GaussianMixture(n_components=4, covariance_type='tied', n_init=1, random_state=1).fit(Xs)
